mechanism_narrative: A low level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the cost of capital and increases equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5% (25th percentile of historical levels).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 3.0% signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises above 3.0% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 0.5% in the prior month signals robust consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS rise by more than 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), a decline in the unemployment rate by more than 0.1 percentage points in the prior month signals improving labor market conditions, which supports consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5.0% and UNRATE declines > 0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0% and declines by more than 0.1% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of monthly payroll growth (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS growth is above 100k (75th percentile of historical monthly growth).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 115 indicates a weakening supply chain and potential economic slowdown, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO falls below 115.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand for housing, which supports construction and related sectors, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST is above 2200 (75th percentile of historical levels).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 3.0% over the past 3 months signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS has been above 3.0% for 3 consecutive months.
